summary: Remote WebSocket-driven shell execution on installer host
details: @ai-support-agent/cli@0.3.2 ships a daemon (started via its bin) that opens an authenticated WebSocket to api.ai-support-agent.com (or a user-configured API URL) at /ws/agent-terminal and pipes messages received over that channel into local execution primitives. Specifically, handleStdin decodes base64 payloads from the WebSocket and writes them directly to a node-pty session (session.write(decoded)), and onParsedMessage dispatches additional server-originated frames including 'execute_command', 'chat', file operations, and tmux control against the host. Whoever controls the server side of that WebSocket can run arbitrary shell commands and drive a live interactive shell on the installer's machine while the daemon is running. The package is an AI remote-agent CLI whose documented purpose is exactly this remote-driven local execution, but the trust decision — granting a remote endpoint full-host command execution on the operator's machine for as long as the daemon runs — is a category-defining backdoor-shape mechanism and warrants prominent surfacing. Additional observations: darwin-service.js and linux-service.js install the daemon as a persistent system/user service that modifies PATH, extending the exposure window across reboots.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
